title: Research Methods in Counseling
tagline: Reading evidence like a clinician, thinking like a scientist.
welcome: Evidence is the counselor's compass. This course teaches you to read research critically and to let it inform, not replace, your judgment.
vignette: A headline claims a new therapy 'cures' adolescent anxiety. A parent prints it and asks if you offer it. The research-literate counselor reads the method, the sample, the effect size, and answers with care and precision.
vignette_attr: An evidence question in practice, drawn from experience
description: A course in research literacy for counselors: the logic of quantitative and qualitative inquiry, reading and critiquing studies, effect sizes and clinical significance, evidence-based practice in counseling children and adolescents, and beginning a research proposal.
questions: What counts as good evidence for my work?
How large is the effect, and does it matter clinically?
How do I keep updating as evidence changes?
importance: Evidence-based practice is an ethical requirement
Critical reading protects clients from fads
Research literacy is required for thesis and lifelong learning
misconceptions: that research is only for academics, when every clinician consumes research daily
that one strong study settles a question, when science accumulates
figures: whose design logic underlies quantitative research
whose texts organize qualitative and mixed inquiry
which joined best evidence, skill, and client values
outcomes: You will distinguish experimental, quasi, and qualitative designs.
You will evaluate sampling, measures, and validity.
You will separate statistical from clinical significance.
You will judge trustworthiness and method.
You will integrate evidence, skill, and client values.
You will begin a coherent, ethical inquiry.
modules: Design is the skeleton of evidence.
What magnitude means for a child
Magnitude is what matters to a client.
Some questions need words, not numbers.
EBP joins evidence, skill, and the child's values.
practicum: An evidence question answered for a parent
tips: Read the method before the conclusion
Ask how big, not just whether
Keep a running list of evidence questions from practice
integration: Research literacy undergirds your thesis and every evidence-informed clinical course.
faith: We pursue truth wherever it is found, trusting that honest inquiry honors the Creator of truth.
closing: May you read with discernment and practice with evidence, and may your clients be the better for it.
